html:
The Rif War was fought from 1921 to 1926 between the Berber tribes of the Rif mountains in northern Morocco, led by Abd el-Krim, and the colonial armies of Spain and later France.

In July 1921 the Rifians routed a Spanish army at Annual, killing thousands of soldiers, one of the worst colonial defeats of the age. Abd el-Krim set up a Republic of the Rif with its own government. Spain answered with bombing, including chemical weapons. In 1925 France joined the war with a huge army.

Abd el-Krim surrendered in 1926 and was exiled. The war shook Spain, helped bring on a military dictatorship, and made the name of young officers such as Francisco Franco. Later guerrilla leaders studied its tactics. See also Spanish Morocco.
sum: The Rif War was fought from 1921 to 1926 between the Berber tribes of the Rif mountains in northern Morocco, led by Abd el-Krim, and the colonial armies of Spain and later France.
